Somos un equipo de desarrolladores de software, amantes de los retos y exploradores del Universo. Buscamos talento que complemente al equipo: artistas gráficos, game developers, creadores de historias o entusiastas de la exploración espacial.

We are a team of software developers, lovers of challenges, and explorers of the universe. We are looking for talent to complement our team: graphic artists, game developers, storytellers, or space exploration enthusiasts.
summary:
Artencio Exploring U is an interactive simulation game where the user designs and directs a complete exploration space mission, inspired by the SLS Artemis program.

The project addresses the challenge by putting the player in the role of an aerospace engineer. To succeed from liftoff to splashdown, the user must make critical decisions regarding the spacecraft's structure, fuel, and thermal shield. In doing so, they manage a randomly assigned budget and face realistic physical and weather variables, experiencing firsthand how each technical choice alters the mission's progression across its two modes (Casual and Real).

This project is important because it transforms the complexity of aerospace engineering—concepts that are often abstract for students—into an accessible and educational experience, interactively demonstrating the delicate balance between safety, performance, and economic viability.
details:
Artencio Exploring U is an exploration space mission simulation video game, inspired by the architecture of the SLS Artemis program. The experience puts the player in the role of an aerospace engineer who must design a spacecraft by making critical decisions regarding its structure, fuel mixture, and thermal shield material, all under the constraints of a randomly generated budget at the start of the game. The game flow covers the complete cycle of a realistic mission: it begins with boarding and pre-launch checks, continues with an orbital ascent governed by precise physics, and concludes with the critical phases of reentry and splashdown on Earth. To accommodate different user profiles, the title offers two exploration modes: a Casual mode, which provides a more flexible margin of error ideal for getting familiar with the mechanics, and a Real mode, which demands absolute precision and simulates the strict conditions of an authentic mission.

The main benefit and the creative factor of this project lie in its high technical fidelity to a real space mission. Unlike a traditional arcade game, our simulator forces the player to balance authentic aerospace engineering variables. The team structured the game considering vital factors such as the ratio of total material weight, thrust efficiency, structural resistance against dynamic pressure (Max Q), and the direct impact of random weather conditions. The intended impact of the project is purely educational and inspiring: it seeks to democratize the understanding of orbital mechanics and interactively demonstrate why space design requires a delicate balance between safety, performance, and economic viability.

To achieve this level of detail, the simulator's architecture was developed using Unity and C#, implementing a rigorous Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) paradigm to handle the complex state machines of the mission and the reading of external data matrices (JSON). Unity allowed us to integrate both the mathematical logic of the flight and the graphical modeling of the environment. Additionally, we ensured an orderly collaborative development and efficient version control by working through Git and GitHub repositories.
